overview.title: The viewpoint that defines Agadir’s skyline
overview.p1: The Kasbah of Agadir Oufella crowns the hill overlooking the bay. Little remains of the old fortress after the 1960 earthquake, but the platform is still the city’s best panorama: beach arc, marina, port and the Anti-Atlas haze inland.
overview.p2: Most visitors come for the view and photos rather than long ruins walks. A short climb or taxi ride brings you to the gate; the light is strongest toward sunset.

food.title: Eat after the viewpoint
food.p1: There is little on the hill itself — plan a meal back in the centre, on the corniche or at the marina after your visit.
food.li2: Corniche cafés for a simple stop.
food.li5: Cash for taxis up and down.

1.title: Getting there
1.desc: Petit taxi from the centre or beach; some walk the road up. Confirm the return fare.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Late afternoon for golden light; mornings are clearer but harsher for photos.

3.title: Site
3.desc: Open viewpoint; mind your step on uneven ground and stay inside marked areas.

q1.question: What is left of the kasbah?
q1.answer: Mostly the hilltop platform and fragments of walls. The draw is the panoramic view over the rebuilt city and bay.

q2.question: How do I get to Kasbah Agadir Oufella?
q2.answer: Petit taxi from the beach or centre is the easiest. The road up is walkable but steep in the heat.

q3.question: Is there an entry fee?
q3.answer: The viewpoint is generally free or has a small site fee — check on arrival.

q4.question: Best time for photos?
q4.answer: Late afternoon and sunset for soft light across the bay.

q5.question: How long do I need?
q5.answer: Forty-five minutes to an hour is enough for the view and photos.
